newsitem.title: NEPAL: Chand survives crucial Nepal vote.
newsitem.headline: Chand survives crucial Nepal vote.

text.p: Prime Minister Lokendra Bahadur Chand survived a crucial test on Wednesday when the Nepali parliament approved a motion of thanks on King Birendra's address to parliament, officials said.
Ram Chandra Poudel, Speaker of the House of Representatives, said the lower house of the Himalayan kingdom's parliament passed the government-backed thanks motion.
The vote signifies the approval of the programmes and policies of Chand's four-month old coalition government, contained in the king's customary address to the parliament.
A similar motion in 1994 failed after rebel deputies of the ruling Nepali Congress abstained, forcing the then Prime Minister Girija Prasad Koirala to resign and call early elections.
The 1994 mid-term elections produced a hung parliament and the communists briefly won power in the world's only Hindu kingdom.
